name: The Gloria Unending

detectability.signature: Chlorophyll-analog absorption bands overlying rhythmic infrared pulses

proximity: Photosynthetic haze dims starfields and scatters active sensor light
Pheromone-like chemical signatures bond to hull exteriors
contact: Filament tendrils adhere to the hull, sampling alloy and paint
Life support intakes clog with respiring spore-matter
prolonged_exposure: Living tissue begins growing across decks, conduits, and crawlspaces
Crew report vivid dreams synchronized with the nebula's breathing

phenomena: Rhythmic photosynthetic pulsing visible across the entire veil
Pheromone-like chemical signatures coating passing hulls
Filament networks conducting light in coordinated patterns
known_incidents: Mining barge Ferrous Daughter spent six weeks inside the veil in 2287; her crew returned healthy, wealthy, and speaking in perfect unison for the rest of their lives.
description: Four astronomical units of photosynthetic haze burn a soft liturgical green-gold, threaded with filaments that pulse in slow unison. Long-range spectroscopy mistakes it for an ordinary emission nebula until the light resolves into rhythms. Within the veil, every grain of dust carries its own living membrane.

The nebula inhales and exhales on an irregular schedule, swelling toward passing ships as if tasting them. Vessels that linger find tendrils adhering gently to their hulls, reading paint, alloy, and skin chemistry. Nothing has yet been digested, but the distinction between curiosity and appetite remains unresolved.

The charter barge Ferrous Daughter spent six weeks inside the Gloria in 2287, and her crew emerged healthy, wealthy, and speaking in perfect unison for the remainder of their lives. The incident made the nebula famous and quietly ended all manned harvesting proposals. Its cells fix metals out of vacuum by methods industrial chemistry cannot reproduce.

The Gloria Unending still breathes at the heart of its empty system, forty million years of patient photosynthesis showing no sign of conclusion. Drone retrievals bring back samples that sing when warmed. Negotiations over what, exactly, the nebula might want remain open.
